fact: DeskEco reports the official launch on 13 June 2026 of the national digital identification system RDC-PASS, led by the Ministry of Digital Economy with technology support from Trident Digital Tech DRC Africa SAS, giving citizens a unique identifier to be used progressively; the President says it is not a national ID card.

Biometric Update reports RDC-Pass was launched as a national digital identity platform, implemented through a 20-year PPP signed June 2025 with Trident Digital Tech DRC Africa SAS and valued at $97.1 million by the Ministry of Planning, with a phased rollout beginning with technical audits and pilot testing.

The Presidency says President Tshisekedi launched the national digital identification system RDC-Pass on 13 June 2026, giving each citizen a unique personal digital identifier, with deployment starting the following Monday and proceeding progressively across the country.

Agence Ecofin reports the ministry presents RDC-PASS, launched in June by President Tshisekedi, as a tool to identify Congolese, now in a first operational phase since September 2026 with 50 enrolment agents trained and rollout to widen gradually.

ONIP handed the first national ID card to the President on 2023-06-30 as the start of a national process; a civil-society group says mass enrolment has not reached provinces such as Tshopo and demands a delivery timetable.

Oeil d'Afrique reports that RDC-PASS, which the government says is not a national identity card but an access key backed by a biometric database, is to be attributed to every Congolese by 2030, with enrolment agents trained on 15 September 2026 and a Kinshasa pilot to follow.

ONIP held its first board meeting on 20-21 August 2026 and defined a roadmap with issuance of the national identity card among its priorities, aiming for a further stage by December (ONIP communique).

ONIP, the DRC national identification office, announced the start of operations of the second national identification of the population coupled with national identity card issuance, to be carried out through a public-private partnership, according to ONIP jurist Serge Mulindwa.
